fields.sample_size: direct interviews and focus group discussions with the District Water and Sanitation Team, WATSAN committees and Water Boards in Sekyere East District, Ghana (about 105 facilities: 69 boreholes, 20 dug wells, 16 piped systems serving 39,643 people, 43% coverage, in five town-area councils)
fields.effect_estimate: Community management of rural water facilities is losing effectiveness: the expected spirit of voluntarism among local managers is fading, they cannot mobilise adequate revenue to cover operation and maintenance partly because households are reluctant to pay and managers lack accountability; orphan boreholes are noted; the authors recommend motivating managers so they are accountable to communities and note a gap between institutional and human-resource capacity and what the SDGs require. Qualitative, one district.
fields.study_design: qualitative single-district case study (interviews and focus groups)
fields.section: Full text: Methods (data from DWST, WATSAN committees and Water Boards); Results (revenue, voluntarism, accountability); Conclusion and recommendations
fields.exact_location: Methods (data from DWST, WATSAN committees and Water Boards); Results (revenue, voluntarism, accountability); Conclusion and recommendations

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative study of community management of rural water facilities in Sekyere East District, Ghana (about 105 facilities, 43% coverage), read in full text 2026-10-04. Fading voluntarism, inadequate revenue and weak accountability undermine O&M. One district.
